reran:
I ran the full `node run.mjs` in a copy at /tmp/s8-review, so the repo was not touched. Setup: Chromium 141.0.7390.37, Node 22.22.2. It took 124 s, in line with the "about 2 minutes" claim.

**Reproduction of the reported numbers**
- Byte-identical to the committed results.json: compat, vmetrics, clip, mixed, bidi, keys, files and haptics.
- Identical across all 8 RTL runs: the FAIL/WARN/INFO summaries and mirror counts. That covers the fixture as served and flipped, and the Bootstrap dashboard and checkout pages as served and flipped.
- Identical seeded scores: as served 14 FAIL / 1 WARN / 9 INFO; flip 16 / 3 / 1 with 4 missed; icons 15/15 and 5/5 as served, 11/15 and 4/5 flipped; 0 false alarms on the good variant.
- auditBaseline reproduces: the good build gets 1 fail, the broken build 0, and the only differing lines are type-size statistics.
- Mobile summaries reproduce: broken portrait 3 FAIL / 7 WARN / 1 INFO; good 0/0/0; Bootstrap checkout-rtl 0 FAIL / 4 WARN.
- Only timings moved: the fixture flip runs took 7.0–7.1 s against 9.1 s reported, and checkout-rtl 369 ms against 872 ms. That is noise.
- No ordering or conclusion changed.

**Spot-checks of the main table values against results.json**
- vmetrics: Tajawal hhea 0.643/0.357 with USE_TYPO_METRICS off; winAscent 1.016.
- Maximum fontkit-vs-canvas difference on Arabic faces: 0.012 em.
- Glyph probe: 53 TP / 0 FP / 4 FN; median 0 px, p90 0.4 px, max 2.2 px.
- The per-component clip table matches.
- Riyal: 3 of 36 families. I re-probed gstatic: Noto Sans, Inter and Plex Arabic return 400; Roboto returns 200.

**Out-of-sample runs of the stream's checkers**
- rtl-check ran on 15 pages it was not built on:
  - Bootstrap album-rtl, blog-rtl and carousel-rtl as served;
  - Bootstrap album, carousel and sidebars flipped;
  - the GOV-SA 2020 dist page, flipped and as served with dir=rtl;
  - tools/regress parity-new, parity-old, capture-reach-rtl and audit-numbers as served;
  - govuk, dashboard and app-traps flipped.
- mobile-check ran on 7 pages: govuk, dashboard, app-traps, album-rtl, offcanvas-navbar, GOV-SA and parity-new.
- There were 0 crashes.

**True positives on the unseen pages**
- Bootstrap carousel-rtl: "© 2017–2026 Company, Inc." shows as "2026–2017".
- parity-old: "+12.4%" is scrambled.
- blog-rtl: italic Arabic headings.
- dashboard flipped: physical `th{text-align:left}`.
- The "RTL adds padding" leak from physical list resets shows up on govuk, GOV-SA and Bootstrap too, so that finding generalises.

The false positives are listed under problems.

**Sources checked**
- Licences are correct:
  - aegov: MIT, from its LICENSE file.
  - riyal font: OFL-1.1, from package.json and LICENSE.txt.
  - vaul: MIT (LICENSE).
  - @base-ui/react 1.8.0: MIT, published 2026-09-04.
  - ios-haptics 3.2.0 and web-haptics 0.0.6: MIT.
  - GOV-SA: GPL-3.0, but only in package.json.
- These [V] claims hold at the stated commits:
  - Radix `getDirectionAwareKey`;
  - React Aria "ArrowLeft always moves to the next tab in RTL";
  - APG has no RTL guidance;
  - Codex: 89 of 293 icons flip, 10 have RTL assets, Help excepts he/yi;
  - Flutter: 76 base icons mirror (I count 2,231 base icons, not 2,235);
  - vaul constants and its "unmaintained" note;
  - Base UI CloseWatcher is Android-only;
  - GOV-SA `[dir="rtl"] * {text-align:right}`;
  - aegov `rtl:-scale-x-100` and drawer `placement:'left'`.
- These BCD 8.1.3 claims hold: vibrate, input switch, VirtualKeyboard, interactive-widget, viewport-fit, CloseWatcher, Navigation, text-justify, ascent-override, match-parent, overflow-x: clip.

problems.claim: audit.mjs addition (d): FAIL on scrambled LTR data in text, detected from Range token order (rtl-check.mjs staticChecks)
problems.problem:
The detector sorts tokens by x across the whole text node and ignores line breaks, so any wrapped English phrase in an RTL block reads as scrambled.
- GOV-SA page as served in RTL: 53 bidi FAILs, e.g. 'Line content' reads as 'content Line' because the td wraps onto 2 lines (confirmed via Range rects).
- govuk --flip: 2 FAILs on the wrapped email error message.
- With a line-aware sort (/tmp/s8-review/rtl-check-patched.mjs), GOV-SA drops to 5 and govuk to 0. The remaining 5 are multi-sentence paragraphs whose punctuation moves; they should be WARNs, but punctuationOnly is still computed on the global order.
- The true positives survive the patch: checkout-rtl '-$5', carousel-rtl '© 2017–2026', parity-old '+12.4%', and the fixture's -310.50.
- None of the fixtures contain wrapped LTR text, so the 24/24 score could not reveal this.
problems.fix: Group tokens by line box (the rect top) and check order within each line only. Compute punctuationOnly per line. Add a fixture with a wrapped English sentence and a wrapped brand name to the regress set before this goes into audit.mjs as a FAIL.

problems.claim: Mobile: 'controls inside the emulated insets: FAIL' (audit.mjs proposal), capture.mjs applying insets by default, and the broken fixture's '8 controls in fixed or sticky bars inside the inset zones'
problems.problem:
mobile-check.mjs FAILs controls under the emulated insets whether or not the page sets viewport-fit=cover (the safe-area FAIL a few lines after the Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride call). The report itself says the CDP override 'applies even without viewport-fit=cover'.
- On iOS without cover, the browser insets the page and env() is 0 [K, WebKit's iPhone X guidance].
- The FAIL fires on Bootstrap offcanvas-navbar's ordinary fixed-top navbar ('navbar-brand top 51px under the status bar/island'). An audit FAIL would hit most sites with a sticky header at phone width.
- The stream's broken fixture has no cover (fixtures/mobile.html line 8). Its headline safe-area FAIL is therefore an emulation artefact, not a defect a real iPhone would show.
- The report also contradicts itself: 'more permissive than iOS' in F5, 'stricter than iOS' in Limits.
problems.fix: Apply insets and raise the FAIL only when the viewport meta has viewport-fit=cover. Without cover, report INFO at most. Rescore the broken fixture with cover set and no env() padding, and fix the wording.

problems.claim: Glyph-extent probe: FAIL on ≥ 1 px ink cut, validated at 53 TP / 0 FP / 4 FN on 126 cases
problems.problem:
The validation used the same 6 faces, 3 strings and 7 recipes the probe was developed on, and none of the cases is a scroll container.
- GOV-SA RTL: 3 false FAILs ('bottom 6px cut') in a scrollable tbody (overflow:auto, scrollHeight 271 > clientHeight 158). The lines straddle the scrollport edge, which is by design; the ink is not clipped.
- The same FAILs appear in flip mode.
- A naive fix that drops lines whose line box crosses the clip edge removed these but also lost a seeded true positive (span.note-text).
problems.fix: Skip lines straddling the edge of a clipper whose overflow is auto or scroll and whose content scrolls (scrollHeight > clientHeight + 1). Keep the rule for hidden, clip and line-clamp. Add scroll-container and real-page cases to the validation set and state that the 126 cases are in-sample.

problems.claim: Matrix: 'aegov tabs: no arrow keys at all [V]'
problems.problem: This is false at d309bb5. js/src/components/custom.js is bundled via index.umd.ts and binds keydown on [data-tabs-toggle] tabs: ArrowRight goes to the next tab in DOM order, ArrowLeft to the previous, and direction is ignored. In RTL that is 'backwards' under the Radix, React Aria and Firefox convention. An Arabic-first government system disagrees with the proposed rule, and the matrix hides that.
problems.fix: Correct the cell. Mark it as a disagreement: aegov uses DOM-order arrows, while Radix, React Aria, Firefox and native Chromium controls follow the visual arrow. Keep FAIL in rtl-check with Firefox's guideline as the source, and note that aegov itself would FAIL.

problems.claim: Volume row: Material '—'; rule 'don't (it belongs to the media cluster)'
problems.problem: Material's bidirectionality text says: 'Icons that hint at a specific direction, like the speaker icon, are mirrored. Other icons, such as a camera and a check mark, remain unmirrored intentionally.' I read it in the English text quoted by github.com/albatrosary/material-design-jp; m*.material.io is blocked here. Codex also flips VolumeUp and VolumeDown. Only Flutter keeps the icon. So 2 of 3 sources mirror volume, and the matrix's rule goes against them. The same Material sentence is also a stronger citation for the checkmark claim.
problems.fix: Set Material to 'mirror (speaker)' and make the volume rule 'record a decision' (the guidance section already says this, but the matrix row does not). Cite the Material sentence for the checkmark row.

problems.claim: F4 line-height floors per face (e.g. Tajawal vocalised 1.65; 'Tajawal overflows its line box by 0.3 em') turned into rules
problems.problem:
Three limits apply.
- **Platform:** the floors come from hhea metrics as used by Chromium on Linux (macOS also uses hhea [K]). Tajawal has USE_TYPO_METRICS off, and Windows DirectWrite uses its winAscent/winDescent (1.016/0.375) [K]. The same arithmetic then gives a vocalised floor of about 1.29, and there is no 0.3 em overflow.
- **Sample size:** one string per category at one size.
- **String content:** the 'vocalised' string has fewer descenders than the 'plain' one (Cairo 1.12 vs 1.27, Almarai 1.30 vs 1.32). Its floors are string-specific, not a superset of plain.
problems.fix: State that the floors assume Linux/macOS (hhea) metrics and that Windows differs for fonts with USE_TYPO_METRICS off. Take max(plain, vocalised) per face. Add a second string per category with kasra and descenders. Present the floors as conservative minima.

problems.claim: rtl-check icon classifier (the NEVER, DIRECTIONAL and AMBIGUOUS regexes), proposed as audit check (f)
problems.problem:
The hand-written lists contradict the matrix's own sources.
- These names are classed 'never', although sources mirror them: star-half (Codex HalfStar flips, Flutter star_half mirrors), user-add/user-plus (Codex UserAdd flips), playlist-add (Flutter mirrors), sort (Flutter mirrors). A correctly mirrored half-star rating would FAIL 'must not mirror'.
- Missed directional icons: chevron-double-right (Bootstrap Icons, Lucide) and box-arrow-up-right (Bootstrap's external link) come out 'unknown'.
- The Arabic context regex for 'next' lacks أكمل ('continue'), so blog-rtl's right-pointing chevron in 'أكمل القراءة' is only a WARN.
problems.fix: Generate the mirror and never-mirror name lists from Codex shouldFlip and Flutter matchTextDirection metadata, plus the matrix. Add the chevron-double-* and box-arrow-* patterns and more Arabic action verbs. Keep unknown icons out of FAIL.

problems.claim: app-ui.md haptics rule 2: '8–15 ms ticks for selection or detents; 25–40 ms for a confirm; at most two pulses'
problems.problem: These numbers carry no source and no grade, yet are written as rules. The Android guidance the report cites says to use the system haptic constants, which the web cannot reach. web-haptics' presets use 25–50 ms. The report also calls web-haptics' SKILL.md a recommendation for 'a haptic on every button press'. That file also lists 'Haptic on every tap (fatigue)' as an anti-pattern and 'Do not overuse'. Its quick reference then maps primary and secondary button taps and 'modal appear' to haptics, so it is self-contradictory, not a plain endorsement.
problems.fix: Tag the durations [K] as a starting point, or drop them in favour of 'short, single, paired with a visual change'. Describe web-haptics as internally inconsistent.

problems.claim: F5 platform table: navigator.share, Firefox '—'; dialog closedby and ascent-override, Safari '—'
problems.problem: BCD 8.1.3 has api.Navigator.share in firefox_android 79 (Firefox desktop 71 behind a flag) and Safari desktop 12.1. dialog closedby and font-face ascent-override are 'preview' in Safari, not absent. The share-sheet guidance ('navigator.share with a copy fallback') survives, but the table is wrong.
problems.fix: Regenerate the table from lib/compat.mjs output instead of writing it by hand, and add the firefox_android and Safari desktop columns.

problems.problem: govuk's visually hidden skip link (1×1 px) is reported as a target under 44 px and as hugging the edge. The 'No viewport-fit=cover' WARN fires on every page tested (app-traps, dashboard, parity-new, album-rtl, GOV-SA). That matches responsive.md's rule but is noise on pages with no fixed bars.
problems.fix: Exclude elements that are clipped or 1×1 until focused. Raise the viewport-fit WARN only when fixed or sticky bars exist; otherwise INFO.

problems.claim: Riyal face '@emran-alhaddad/saudi-riyal-font' maps A, B, C, D and U+E900; fetch.sh: 'The API answers 400 when the family has no glyph'
problems.problem: fontkit on the woff2 shows it also maps U+20C0 (SOM SIGN) and U+E001/E002. Loaded without unicode-range, it would draw a riyal where Kyrgyz som text appears. As for the probe: the CSS API returned an @font-face (HTTP 200) for all 36 families. It is the gstatic kit URL that returns 400 for families without the glyph (re-checked: Noto Sans, Inter and Plex Arabic give 400, Roboto 200). The conclusion stands, but the method description is wrong.
problems.fix: List U+20C0 in the report and keep unicode-range: U+20C1 mandatory. Correct the comment in fetch.sh.

problems.problem:
- GOV-SA's GPL-3.0 comes from package.json only; the repo has no LICENSE file.
- 'dir="auto" on an empty field resolves to ltr in Chromium' is HTML-spec behaviour for every engine, not a Chromium quirk.
- `overflow-x:clip` with `text-overflow:ellipsis` '(Safari 16+)': BCD confirms only overflow-x:clip support; the ellipsis combination is unverified in WebKit.
- The inline `:lang(ar){line-height:1}` fix 'works everywhere' was measured only in Chromium, and it lets mark ink overlap neighbouring lines.
- Sheet dismiss thresholds 'per vaul (0.4 px/ms or 25%)' are defaults from an unmaintained library, not UX evidence, even while the report advises against vaul.
problems.fix: Tag each of these accordingly: licence per package.json; spec behaviour; WebKit unverified; Chromium-only; one implementation's defaults.
Add short matrix rows for label alignment, validation icons and swipe direction. Mark the other items as not covered, so the merge does not assume they were researched.

weakest:
**Rules built on unmeasured numbers:**
- The thumb-reach WARN rests on a heuristic model whose parameters were not measured. Its one conclusion only restates ui-ux.md's 'lower two-thirds'.
- The keyboard-open check models the keyboard as 336 px [K].
- The haptic durations of 8–15 ms and 25–40 ms have no source.

**Checks that misfire on unseen pages:**
- The safe-area FAIL fires on pages without viewport-fit=cover, so it is an emulation artefact.
- The scramble detector as a FAIL gave 48 false FAILs of 53 on a real RTL page, from wrapped lines.
- The glyph probe FAILs on scrollable containers.
- The hand-written icon regexes FAIL icons the matrix's own sources mirror (star-half, user-add, playlist).

**Sample-bound or partly misread sources:**
- The per-face line-height floors come from one string per category, one engine and Linux hhea metrics; Tajawal differs on Windows.
- The size-adjust ranges by script structure come from one measurement method.
- The Material and Apple columns rest on search snippets, and one of them was misread: Material mirrors the speaker icon.
- The aegov 'no arrow keys' claim is false.
- The DGA rules come through a third-party transcription.

**In-sample validation:** the 24/24 seeded-defect score and the 126-case probe validation were both measured on the fixtures the scripts were built against. They show capability, not precision.
